articles.title: Filmed at a Scottish castle, the TV series The Traitors has generated £21.8 million for Scotland’s economy and supported more than 750 jobs since production began in 2022, report finds
articles.summary: The BBC’s The Traitors, filmed at Ardross Castle in the Scottish Highlands, has contributed an estimated £21.8 million in Gross Value Added (GVA) to
articles.body: The BBC’s The Traitors, filmed at Ardross Castle in the Scottish Highlands, has contributed an estimated £21.8 million in Gross Value Added (GVA) to Scotland’s economy between 2022 and 2025. The Traitors: Scotland Economic Impact says the show format has supported over 750 workforce jobs, an average of 189 a year. According to the BBC report, every £1 of GVA directly generated by the production meant a total of £6.84 was added to the Scottish economy. Nine series have been filmed at the castle since 2022, with four more confirmed for 2026.How did BBC's The Traitors generate £21.8 million for the Scottish economyThe Traitors contributed £21.8 million in Gross Value Added (GVA) to the Scottish economy between 2022 and 2025. It says this reflects direct production spending as well as indirect effects across sectors such as hospitality, transport and local services, and the induced effect of spending by workers in the local economy. Every £1 of GVA directly generated by the production meant a total of £6.84 was added to the Scottish economy.On employment, the report says the show supported over 750 workforce jobs across all series produced between 2022 and 2025, an average of 189 jobs per year. The actual number of roles created is likely to be higher because the programme is in production for only a few weeks of the year. The report adds that for every job directly working on the production in Scotland, a further 14.8 jobs were created across the wider Scottish economy through spending with local suppliers. It also reports that the production period was 17 weeks in 2025 and is set to increase to 25 weeks in 2026, owing to the commissioning of an additional US series for NBCU.How has The Traitors boosted Scotland's screen tourism sectorThe Traitors is strengthening Scotland's existing screen tourism sector. It cites research commissioned by Screen Scotland that estimated £140 million of GVA was added to Scotland's economy in 2023 through tourism expenditure associated with screen tourism, a figure that relates to screen tourism as a whole rather than to the show alone. Among the figures are a 190% rise in Expedia searches for the Highlands following series two, a 69% rise in Trainline bookings to Inverness since the show began, and a 60% increase in SIXT-reported Google searches for "castle holidays" over January 2025. Tour operator EvanEvan reported a 44% rise in Edinburgh-related searches and a 27% increase in Scotland-wide searches in the first three weeks of January 2025.According to the VisitScotland, during the celebrity series, searches including "Traitors castle", "Where is the Traitors castle?" and "Where is Traitors filmed?" were between 17% and 33% above 2025's previous high. It states that the castle is not open to the public and that Ardross Castle is privately owned. VisitScotland says it has run themed content across social media and its website, and sent an email to around 289,000 subscribers ahead of the finale. US visitors accounted for 22% of all overseas trips to Scotland and 36% of all overseas spending in 2024, citing VisitScotland analysis of the International Passenger Survey.Traitors contribute to Scotland's audiovisual sectorThe report says Ardross Castle, which operates as an events venue, has seen a fourfold increase in enquiries, which it attributes to the show's public profile, and is now fully booked each year. It quotes Ardross Castle director Loukas Tsarmaklis as saying the production has brought business to local taxis, shops, building suppliers, wholesale suppliers and hotels, mainly around Alness and Inverness. The report also states that 20% of the total economic impact between 2022 and 2025, over £4 million in GVA, is felt within Scotland's audiovisual sector.On production status, the foreword by Hayley Valentine, Director of BBC Scotland, says the show qualifies as a Scottish production under Ofcom's rules because it is made from a production base in Scotland and over half the spend on the production team goes to people living outside London. The report states that series one and two of the BBC's The Traitors qualified as Made out of London productions, and that the NBCU series, which make up roughly half of the commissioning volume, are not required to meet the same criteria. It also records that interviewees pointed to ongoing challenges, including the need for more studio space and post-production facilities in the Highlands, and the lack of clear pathways to long-term employment. The report concludes that the show "has proven to be a landmark production for Scotland". It also says Screen Scotland, Studio Lambert and the BBC have created training placements, and that spillover effects were acknowledged qualitatively but not quantified.You use AI every day. articles.title: Jay-Z and his mother built a scholarship foundation for students facing financial barriers; it reports more than 2,700 awards since inception, including 324 during the 2025-26 academic year
articles.summary: For more than two decades, Shawn “Jay-Z” Carter and his mother, Dr Gloria Carter, have worked to remove one of the biggest obstacles between talented
articles.body: For more than two decades, Shawn “Jay-Z” Carter and his mother, Dr Gloria Carter, have worked to remove one of the biggest obstacles between talented young people and higher education: Money. Their Shawn Carter Foundation says it has now made more than 2,700 scholarship awards since it began, including 324 awards during the 2025-26 academic year. The figures, shared through the foundation’s newsletter, underline how a family-led effort launched in 2003 has grown into a sustained national support system for students facing economic hardship. Read more details about it here:A foundation born from experienceThe Shawn Carter Foundation was founded by Jay-Z and Gloria Carter in 2003 with a clear purpose: To help motivated students who lack the financial means to pursue education beyond high school. Gloria Carter has been central to the organisation’s mission, arguing that many capable young people are overlooked because their grades, circumstances or family finances do not fit conventional scholarship models.The foundation was created on the belief that financial need should not determine whether a person can continue learning. Its programmes have expanded beyond direct scholarships to include college preparation, professional development, scholar support, international exposure and community initiatives. That broader approach reflects the Carters’ view that education is not only about paying tuition, but also about giving students the tools to finish what they start.What the scholarship coversThe foundation’s National Scholarship Fund is designed to support students from admission through graduation. According to the foundation, qualifying students can receive up to $15,000 over the course of their studies, with the money available for tuition and practical necessities such as transportation, food, laundry, clothing and other essentials. That flexibility matters because the cost of college is rarely limited to tuition. Students may need help with books, travel, lab fees or everyday living expenses, and a scholarship that addresses those pressures can make the difference between staying enrolled and dropping out. The foundation has also historically paid awards directly to educational institutions to help ensure the money supports students’ education.More than 2,700 awardsThe latest reported milestone is substantial: more than 2,700 awards since the foundation’s inception. Of those, 324 were awarded in the 2025-26 academic year, a figure that shows the programme’s continued reach at a time when many families remain under pressure from rising education and living costs.The foundation has long focused on students who may not qualify for more traditional merit-based aid. Eligibility has included high school seniors, GED holders, undergraduate students and those attending vocational or trade schools, with financial need considered alongside factors such as leadership, community service and personal resilience. The programme has also welcomed students who might have lower grade-point averages but still demonstrate determination and potential.Scholars are asked to give backA distinctive part of the Shawn Carter Foundation model is its expectation that recipients contribute to others. Scholars are required to take part in community service and to mentor younger aspiring students, creating a cycle in which today’s beneficiaries can help open doors for tomorrow’s applicants.That requirement turns the scholarship into more than a financial transaction. It encourages students to see themselves as part of a wider community and to use their education as a platform for service. For many recipients, mentoring younger students may also provide practical guidance about applications, college life and the challenges of balancing study with financial pressures.Support beyond the chequeWhile scholarships remain the foundation’s best-known work, its activities extend further. The organisation has supported college tours, including visits to historically Black colleges and universities, as well as study-abroad opportunities and wealth-building programmes for young people and families. These initiatives are intended to widen students’ sense of what is possible after high school.Jay Z's mother, Dr Gloria Carter, has described education as the key to unlocking opportunity, a principle that runs through the foundation’s scholarship and community programmes, as per a report by Parade on Yahoo! The organisation’s work has also attracted major philanthropic support, with its 20th-anniversary gala reported to have raised $20 million in a single night.Why the milestone mattersReaching more than 2,700 awards is not just a number. It represents thousands of individual decisions to continue studying despite financial uncertainty, and hundreds of families who received practical help at a critical moment. The 324 awards made in 2025-26 suggest that the foundation remains active and focused on expanding access rather than treating its early success as a finished project.For students considering higher education, the foundation’s message is straightforward: financial barriers are real, but they do not have to be permanent. By combining direct funding with mentoring, community service and broader development programmes, Jay-Z and Dr. Gloria Carter have built a scholarship model designed not only to help students enrol, but to help them persist, graduate and pass opportunity forward.You use AI every day. articles.title: SC on Diwali: Crackers on Nov 7-8 in 2 time slots, and keep it green
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Holding that Deepawali has a religious, social, psychological and emotional significance for people, Supreme Court on Monday kept the window
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Holding that Deepawali has a religious, social, psychological and emotional significance for people, Supreme Court on Monday kept the window open for bursting of green firecrackers on Nov 7 and 8 between 6am and 7am, and between 8pm and 10pm.The court had allowed bursting of crackers at the same time last year too.A bench of Justices M M Sundresh and Prasanna B Varale directed police and administration to ensure polluting crackers remain out of bounds for people in Delhi, and take punitive action against those who deal in such crackers.While acknowledging Deepawali's significance, the court stressed that the right of an individual to engage in a particular practice, which may have a religious colour, was only a qualified one and not exempt from restrictions allowed by the Constitution."...Allowing the environment to degrade, which results in a health hazard to all living beings, defeats the very purpose of the festivities... All parties before us are ad idem (of one mind) on the fact that bursting of firecrackers is contributing enormously to pollution in Delhi/NCR," it said. Restriction on manufacture and sale of crackers in the national capital will continue after Diwali.The bench, however, did not favour a complete ban on firecrackers. “Though imposition of a blanket ban seems to be the ideal solution, we are of the opinion that this court, at this point in time, is short of adequate data to decide whether or not a complete ban would be the best solution to solve the problem of environmental pollution, caused by bursting firecrackers,” it said.The bench directed district collectors/commissioners, in consultation with the superintendent of police concerned, to identify and designate locations in the NCR to facilitate the sale of green crackers and banned online sale. “The sale of firecrackers shall be strictly prohibited in any other location, other than the designated ones, including sale through online platforms,” it said.“We direct the authorities concerned to mandate all manufacturers and traders of firecrackers in Delhi-NCR to furnish a monetary security, which shall be a handsome amount, as determined by them. The said security deposit shall immediately stand forfeited in case any manufacturer or trader of firecrackers violates any of the directions passed by this court,” the bench said.The court noted in its order that bursting of firecrackers, though constituting a religious practice meant to celebrate the occasion, would result in severe environmental pollution, especially air and noise, apart from the creation of solid waste. It said the unregulated practice affected everyone, including the end user and, among human beings, children, disabled and elderly people constituted the most vulnerable groups.“It is not in dispute that the right to practice, profess and propagate religion conferred under Article 25(1) of the Constitution is certainly subject to public order, morality, health and other provisions of Part III of the Constitution. This court has repeatedly held that ‘right to life’ envisaged under Article 21 of the Constitution includes the right to a healthy, safe and pollution-free environment, and the said position has been crystallised and, hence, requires no repetition. Therefore, the right of an individual to engage in a particular practice, which may have a religious colour, is only a qualified one and cannot go beyond constitutional restrictions,” the bench said.It added that there shall be no manufacture or sale of firecrackers joined in series (‘ladis’) and garlands. Use of firecrackers with barium and those not approved by CSIRNEERI as green crackers shall not be permitted.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Do the Shetland Isles need Cold War-style military protection?
articles.summary: Calls are being made for the defence of the Shetland Isles to be strengthened after increased sightings of Russian trawlers off the coast of Scotland.
articles.body:
Calls are being made for the defence of the Shetland Isles to be strengthened after increased sightings of Russian trawlers off the coast of Scotland.

Recent analysis by the Daily Telegraph also revealed that there have been more than 500 incidents where Russian boats have been stationed above undersea cables linking Britain with Europe and the US.

These cables carry the majority of telecoms data abroad.

The growing importance of undersea infrastructure prompted a parliamentary report last year to warn of security vulnerabilities in areas including transport and supply chains, financial services and payment systems.

There are also concerns that the £30m SaxaVord Spaceport in Shetland could be a Russian target.

But do the Shetland Isles really need better protection by the military?

In recent years there have been a number of incidents in the Baltic Sea where underwater cables have been damaged or completely cut.

In December last year, Finnish police detained a vessel sailing from Russia, which was suspected of damaging an undersea telecoms cable running from Helsinki to Estonia, across the Gulf of Finland.

In 2022, Shetland was cut off from the mainland after a nearby subsea cable was damaged .

And last year there were two cable breaks in Shetland , which disrupted internet services and, in one case, took weeks to repair.

There has been no suggestion that there was any Russian involvement in the Shetland incidents but they demonstrate how fragile the cables are and show the devastating effect on the islanders when they are damaged.

In July, Royal Navy warships and helicopters spent 21 days monitoring Russian activity in UK waters and the North Atlantic - this was a 25% increase on previous time spent monitoring.

The recent Telegraph revelation of more than 500 incidents where Russian boats have been stationed above undersea cables has also caused concern.

What is the history of Shetland's defences?

Jon Sandison, a high school history teacher and Shetland tour guide, said there were real concerns that Shetland could be attacked after Germany invaded Norway in 1940, during World War Two.

"Shetland could have been a stepping stone towards Orkney and mainland Scotland," he said.

There were many army, naval and RAF personnel stationed across the isles and coastal defences were built to defend Lerwick and the rest of the archipelago.

The SaxaVord Spaceport sits on a former RAF base and RAF Skaw played an important role in efforts to detect enemy aircraft from 1941.

RAF Saxa Vord was later involved in Nato's radar network to monitor Soviet activity during the Cold War.

The radar station closed in 2006 but it was revived in 2018 for Arctic surveillance as an automated remote radar head.

Sandison said that while military presence reduced in the second half of the 20th Century, Shetland's geographical position would never change.

"Where we are in the UK is always going to be a pivotal geographical location in relation to the North Sea, the Arctic Circle and wider scope of Britain," he said.

He added that coastal infrastructure was built very quickly during the Second World War.

"Air raid shelters, anti-aircraft defences - it's remarkable how much was built in a short space of time," he added.

"Not much of the infrastructure remains. It's part of our history, and part of our past."

First Minister John Swinney has accused the UK government of leaving "Scotland's vast coastline dangerously exposed".

He pointed to waters off Shetland as an area of significant Russian activity.

"I don't think we've got nearly the presence in those areas that we require today," he told BBC Scotland News .

Liberal Democrat MP Alistair Carmichael, whose constituency covers Shetland, has urged the UK government to step up efforts to protect critical infrastructure.

He told the BBC's Radio Scotland Breakfast programme: "This is something we do need to be taking seriously.

"We're not expecting an imminent problem here but this is a time where the government is already telling us that we should all be keeping baked beans and a wind-up torch in a cupboard."

I do not have confidence UK is safe from Russian threats - Swinney

Damaged cable cuts Shetland off from mainland

Carmichael added that if the world had changed so much, some of the decisions made by the UK government to remove military presence from the northern isles may now need to be looked at again.

He said that over the last 20 years, there had been just one local full-time soldier running a reserved unit in Shetland but they were now managed from the Scottish mainland.

Carmichael said there should be restoration of a full-time presence to support the unit and more reserves should be recruited in the northern isles as numbers were low.

But he added: "If the signal that the government is sending the community is that we don't even think its important enough to send one full-time solider to run these units then you can't expect the community themselves to be particularly enthusiastic about it."

What is the significance of the spaceport?

SaxaVord in Unst is the UK's first fully-licensed spaceport with several companies interested in using the site to launch small satellites into orbit.

In September, the UK government announced investment of £30m in the project, as part of a new £7.8bn space strategy.

Alistair Carmichael said the spaceport would draw more attention to Shetland as a significant asset.

The German and UK governments plan to use SaxaVord to deepen their co-operation on space .

In October, Prime Minister Andy Burnham and Chancellor Friedrich Merz met in Berlin and announced plans to work more closely on economic growth, defence and technology.

SaxaVord Spaceport was identified as a focus for immediate work on European launches.

Two German companies are currently in a race to be the first to test a rocket in Shetland.

Chief executive Scott Hammond said: "The space strategy is absolutely critical.

"We're at the heart of the UK government's plans for assured access to space.

"That's also for our economic and Nato partners."

He added that the UK government had joined as one of its majority investors, with a member on the board, but stressed that SaxaVord Spaceport was still a private commercial company.

A Ministry of Defence spokesperson said: "We are clear-eyed about the threat Russia poses.

"Through the UK-led Joint Expeditionary Force, we are leading allied activity across the High North, strengthening Nato's northern flank and increasing our ability to respond rapidly to emerging threats.

"This government is also investing in the capabilities needed to meet those threats, with £1.5bn backing Atlantic Bastion to deliver a next-generation Hybrid Navy and a further £330m to strengthen the protection of critical undersea infrastructure."

articles.body: A 20-year-old aspiring airline pilot and a Texas couple traveling with their two young children are among the nine people killed when a private jet plunged into a South Florida neighborhood Sunday. The Learjet 60 departed Austin-Bergstrom International Airport at about 10:37 a.m. and was headed to North Eleuthera in the Bahamas when it crashed in Palm Beach County shortly before 1 p.m., killing everyone on board. Federal investigators said Monday that weather conditions are a "major focus" of the investigation after the crew reported icing and moderate turbulence at about 35,000 feet shortly before the jet rapidly lost altitude.
